thread:
emily-support: FYI AcmePay reporting ~30% "Invalid JSON" errors from /v1/generate-orders this morning. They say it began after last night's model deploy.

raj-ml: can you share a failing request_id and the raw model output + model/params?

emily-support: request_id=rid_2040012_07, model=redwood-lite-v1.1, temp=0.0, json_mode=strict

emily-support: sample client payload (trimmed, described): orders array with three items: item1 sku_123 qty=2 line_id=L1; item2 sku_456 qty=1 temp_id=t-789 (client-side temporary id); item3 sku_999 qty=3.

emily-support: raw model response we received (literal text): contains trailing commas after objects, a dangling comma before the array end, and the second order lacks the canonical line_id and only includes temp_id. Parser fails.

sarah-eng: that output has multiple problems — trailing commas, duplicated/heterogeneous object shapes, and missing canonical ids. strict JSON parser will fail with errors like "Expecting property name enclosed in double quotes".

kyle-support: customer saw ~422 parse failures and intermittent 500s. Also observed a spike in 401 auth errors in the same window — their CI rotates tokens every 5 minutes; we logged ~10 401s then immediate retries which inflated billing.

deploy-bot: rolling-deploy redwood-lite-v1 -> v1.1 at 2024-09-26T11:20:13Z (config change: default json_mode="strict").

raj-ml: hypotheses:
- v1.1 made default json_mode stricter, so previously tolerated outputs now fail.
- client uses temp_id locally until backend assigns line_id; model sometimes echoes temp_id instead of canonical line_id -> partial objects.
- token rotation + aggressive client retries caused duplicated work and billing anomalies.

sarah-eng: eng-runtime needs a repro. please paste a minimal curl with headers (Authorization placeholder) so runtime can reproduce against hosted API.

kyle-support: repro curl (sanitized, payload described rather than full JSON to avoid copy issues):
  curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate-orders \n    -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \n    -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n    -d '<orders payload: item1 with line_id L1, item2 with temp_id t-789>'

kyle-support: expected: well-formed JSON array where each order has line_id (or explicit null). actual: mixed keys and trailing commas caused parser error. streaming responses also produced chunk-boundary errors like "Unexpected end of JSON input at chunk 2" when the response was streamed and an object was split across chunks.

sarah-eng: short-term mitigation: set json_mode=relaxed for affected tenant to accept trailing commas and missing fields; add lightweight pre-parse fixer to normalize trailing commas and map temp_id->line_id when mapping exists. Long-term: runtime should sanitize model outputs before handing to parser and ML should avoid echoing client temp ids for canonical fields.

raj-ml: logs for rid_2040012_07 and rid_2040012_09 attached to INC-2040012. timestamp window: 2040012350 - 2040012370 UTC.

emily-support: customer requests RCA + credits for retries causing billing spike. escalating to billing.

oncall: taking this. will audit token rotation logs and retry spikes; coordinating with billing and eng-runtime.

sarah-eng: action items:
- eng-runtime: implement a sanitizer that either auto-fixes (remove trailing commas, join split chunks) or rejects and emits clear telemetry when model outputs unknown/extra keys. Also buffer stream chunk boundaries to avoid mid-object parses.
- ml: investigate why model echoes temp_id instead of producing canonical line_id for subsequent items.
- support/billing: review chargebacks for retries between 2040012350-2040012370.
- devex: update streaming guidance in docs and recommend client-side tolerant merge logic for temp ids.

kyle-support: note: streaming boundaries are a reproducible separate failure vector; runtime buffering/final-assembly is required to guarantee valid JSON for strict mode.

raj-ml: filing INC-2040012 and assigning to eng-runtime; will follow up with repro harness output.

emily-support: customer looped into ticket, they appreciate the quick triage. :thumbsup:
